decisions.reason: Definition (b) composed a Euclidean-domain u with the quotient q:R^3→T^3, an undefined map. Replaced it by torus maps u with periodic pullbacks u∘q and the unique descent u([x])=ũ(x); derivatives descend because translations preserve their values. Measure, Fourier normalization and integer weak Sobolev orders are unchanged.

The complex Fourier inverse in proof 3.1 omitted the reality check needed for real H^s. Added conjugate symmetry a_{−k}=conj(a_k) and injectivity to prove wα=conj(wα) componentwise; also made complex character testing the sum of real and imaginary test identities. The derivative and norm claims remain unchanged.

The alleged strengthened constants are proved explicitly in the cited supplier: proof 1.2 gives 4^(−s)(1+|k|²)^s≤q_k≤(s+1)^3(1+|k|²)^s and proof 2.2 sums them by Parseval. Thus L1 states an actual established consequence of that dependency, not an unlicensed hypothesis. Checked the lattice shell estimate, uniform differentiated convergence and the separate integer-gap Holder endpoints; no repair is needed.

The upper Fourier-tail estimate was valid but title sharpness lacked a lower bound. Added u=cos(nx¹), N=n−1, giving the squared derivative-norm ratio ≥1/((s+1)n²), which excludes a uniform o(N^(−1)) rate. Self-adjointness, derivative commutation and contraction follow directly from the finite symmetric Fourier ball. Statement unchanged.

The workspace defines only integer Sobolev orders and the embedding theorem assumes integer s,m. There are no admissible gaps 1<s−m≤3/2. The stated H¹→C⁰ counterclaim is refuted by the real symmetric shells with C⁰/H¹≥c2^(N/2); integer gap 2 is allowed by the supplier. Sharpness here is within that integer scale, not an assertion about undefined fractional H^s. No repair needed.

L3 misattributed the chain and Leibniz rules to a notation-only definition. Added the actual published total chain rule, continuous-partials differentiability theorem and one-variable general Leibniz rule, explicitly deriving the multi-index rule by coordinate iteration. Checked all product-order cases, cutoff extension for nonconvex O, density and high estimates n≥6. Stated integer s,n explicitly, consistent with the existing Sobolev definition.

There is no declared reverse deps edge, but Definition (e) used E,B via the later Weyl definition, creating a concealed formulation dependence on its own consumer. Defined E,B locally as independent symmetric spatial trace-free tensors and removed later-result premises from Definition. Their later reconstruction and constrained-curvature interpretation remain intact; tentative connection and tilted gauge conventions are unchanged.

The statement omitted explicit integrality in (b), although only integer H^s is defined. Added integer s to (b) and the given data; (c) inherits it. Tail compactness uses finite-dimensional compact closure and deterministic least-index selections; the rational extraction applies with r=s and the Banach FTC gives uniform Lipschitz continuity. No fractional-order extension was intended or proved.

A derivative bound on a disconnected set does not control the energy between components. Required J to be an interval, so every segment from t₀ to t stays in the bounds; made the existing integer Sobolev convention explicit. Checked self-adjoint projected differentiation, symmetric integration by parts and commutator/time derivative bounds, which give |e′|≤C(1+e) and oriented Gronwall.

The missing equivalence theorem is unnecessary here: the Counterexample itself differentiates T^(00),T^(0i),T^(ij) and directly writes ∂_a δT^(ab)=0, obtaining f_t+H₀div v=0 and H₀v_t−a²grad f=0. Equally these follow by differentiating the equations explicitly defined in clause (c) of the cited fluid model. The mode ODE and smooth e^(−sqrt(n)) datum prove only the stated fixed-flat linearized failures, with no nonlinear inference. No repair needed.

The title and closing reference promised transformed fluid equations that were absent. Added the two reversible equations u·∇r+c_s div u=0 and ∇_u u+c_s(g⁻¹+u⊗u)dr=0, deriving them with r′=c_s/(ε+p) and dp=c_s²dε; both divisions are positive on J. The integral is smooth, strictly increasing and has a smooth one-dimensional inverse; detailed positive symbol remains the consuming lemma.
